text: User decision (2026-10-02): package, import and CLI renamed from airec-client/airec_client to plain 'airec', with no compatibility alias. Not to be published to PyPI yet. Note: an unrelated experimental 'airec' 0.1.0 already exists on PyPI (see docs/research/app-analysis.md), so the name will clash when publishing is considered.

User decisions (2026-10-02): bulk sync skips recordings by local filename only (no size check). Sync stops at the first failure with no automatic retry; the user reruns it. Opt-in --delete-after --yes deletes only recordings this run downloaded and published, never ones that were already local. Progress is reported per file only. Sync refuses an active or paused recording unless --stop-recording is given. If the firmware does not honor the 0x07 offset, resume is dropped, not worked around. Resume keeps the no-partial-success invariant: partial bytes appear only on a DownloadInterrupted error, never as a return value.

User decision (2026-10-02): read-only device queries (0x12, 0x29, 0x20, 0x36, 0x26) are in scope. Never expose 0x64, because it returns the stored Wi-Fi SSID and password. Superseded in part (later on 2026-10-02): setting writes are now in scope for six single-value setters (0x18, 0x19, 0x22, 0x2a, 0x2e, 0x39), only if payloads are confirmed by app research AND a live probe; 0x24 (toggle) and 0x23 stay excluded. Writes require stopped state, send once, verify by 0x26 read-back, no retry.

Observed 2026-10-02: .venv once had the upstream PyPI 'airec' 0.1.0 and a stale 'airec_client' editable install. The upstream package hid src/airec, so 'python -m airec' failed and tests could run against the wrong code. If imports behave strangely, check 'pip list' first. User preference: keep all APK and reverse-engineering exploration (extracted APK, Blutter build, probes, findings) under the ignored artifacts/ directory, currently artifacts/re/.

Observed 2026-10-02 on the user's recorder: 6 of 11 archives had a size that is not a multiple of 80 bytes. Each ended with a truncated final Opus slot (remainders of 32, 48 and 64 bytes). The two archives in the first validation were both aligned, which hid this. Lesson: validate audio handling against a full real catalog, not one or two files. During the live tests the recorder also dropped connections intermittently (about 4 times; RSSI about -80 dBm) and was sometimes not advertising until power-cycled. Power-on recording is enabled on this device, so each power cycle starts a recording that must be stopped before downloads work.

User intent (2026-10-02): the next features, in this order: (1) device setting writes, mainly turning off power-on recording (ticket oa-pshdj); (2) Wi-Fi fast transfer (oa-mkioh); (3) live audio stream (oa-mzdbt). The tickets carry what is known and are NOT approved; plan each one with the user first. Concern to raise when planning Wi-Fi: the user's only recorder reports work mode 1 (jl + ble), so Wi-Fi cannot be validated on hardware.

How live work went on 2026-10-02. Recorder control: the user stops recordings with the device button when asked. Do not stop recordings from the client unless the user approves it. The phone app was kept disconnected. If the recorder does not advertise, ask the user to power it on, which starts a recording (power-on recording is on). Proven probe pattern: a one-off script under artifacts/re/ that uses client internals, writes JSON output to artifacts/re/probe_output/, and is never committed. Reverse engineering: the APK is at artifacts/temp/*.apk. Blutter (with capstone built from source in artifacts/re/deps) already produced artifacts/re/out/ (asm per Dart file, pp.txt object pool, objs.txt). artifacts/re/tools/slim.py filters asm lines. artifacts/re/findings.md is the full app 2.1.3 report. Dart Smi values are tagged (x2) in compares. Opcode keys are in protocol/command/key_profiles.dart. If @developer fails with 'model unavailable', its agent config needs fixing; the user fixes that.

User decision (2026-10-02): no Wi-Fi transfer code, because the user's only recorder is work mode 1 (jl + ble) and cannot validate it. Rejected: an unvalidated implementation gated on work modes 6-10. Wi-Fi findings are moved into docs/research/ instead (ticket oa-jkwch).

User decision (2026-10-02): live audio is research-first (static app analysis, then a live probe that sends 0x6d once and always 0x6e on exit). The API is planned only after the packet format is known. The ordering dependency on the Wi-Fi ticket was dropped.

User decisions (2026-10-02): setting writes do not require an ack, because hardware showed 0x2a and 0x2e send no reply while 0x18/0x22/0x39 echo the opcode. The 0x26 read-back is the only proof of success. Rejected: per-setter ack rules (more rules, no extra safety). Noise reduction 0x19 was dropped: no effect on the user's firmware. Accepted ranges: mic gain 1-7, segment duration 1-600 min, idle shutdown 1-525600 min.

User decision (2026-10-02): do not change the recording format with 0x79 on the user's recorder. Reasons: the app sends 0x79 only for chipType 8, knows only 00 WAV / 01 MP3 (no Opus value), so a work mode 1 recorder might not return to Opus; WAV would be about 8x larger and slower to download; the library assumes 80-byte Opus. The R2 live probe (ticket oa-kyysf) was closed without running. Research is in docs/research/record-type.md.
